newsitem.title: UK: UK said targetting single parents on welfare.
newsitem.headline: UK said targetting single parents on welfare.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair is set to announce a major welfare reform under which up to 800,000 jobless single parents will be hauled into unemployment offices to be found work, the Observer paper reported on Sunday.

The Observer and other newspapers said Blair would unveil his plans in a speech on Monday detailing ways to slash Britain's massive welfare bill, which now stands at just below 100 billion pounds ($160 billion) a year.
"Fatalism is as big a problem as poverty, the deadening weight of low expectations and the debilitating belief that things cannot get better," the Sunday Telegraph quoted Blair as planning to say.
"I want to give people back their self-belief and the will to win again. But that means being tough on poor teachers and tough on those who are offered the chance to work but do not want to take it."
A government spokeswoman declined to comment on the reports, saying Blair was still working on his speech.

Welfare reform is crucial if Blair's Labour Party, elected in a landslide on May 1, is to achieve its pledge to keep within the tight public spending limits set by the outgoing Conservative government for the next two years.

Blair discussed tough U.S. back-to-work schemes when he met President Bill Clinton last Thursday. One U.S. idea which could be introduced is the "single mother's club" where parents can leave their children under supervision.
Under other proposals, single parents would lose benefits unless they made themselves available for work or training as soon as their youngest child started school.

The spokeswoman said official figures showed that 4.5 millon Britons lived in families where no one worked, one million Britons had never worked since leaving school and Britain had more single parents than any other European Union nation.
Labour has pledged to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities to get 250,000 people off welfare and into work.
A few days after the election, newspapers reported that Labour planned to provide free child care for a million single mothers to help them to find work.
